the_wrong_statements.the_label: the capability probe that was run before the batch

the_recorded_text.what_it_was: one plain 'sleep 6' command issued with the tool timeout 5000 ms BEFORE any command of the batch
the_recorded_text.why: the plan requires that the tool accepts and enforces the frozen cap of 5000 ms, and that the executor stops before the execution instead of falling back when the tool cannot take it
the_recorded_text.what_happened: the tool accepted the value 5000 and cut the command off at its 5 second cap and moved it to the background, which proves that the cap is accepted and enforced and that it is not silently raised to the 30000 ms value of the previous batch
the_recorded_text.what_it_touched: nothing: the probe ran no candidate code, it imported nothing, it compiled nothing, it collected nothing, it ran no test, it wrote no file, it opened no network and it touched neither the counter nor the report root
the_recorded_text.the_residue: the backgrounded sleep finished on its own a moment later; it left nothing behind

the_wrong_statements.why_it_is_wrong: the recorded text says that the tool 'cut the command off at its 5 second cap' and that this 'proves that the cap is accepted and enforced'.  The tool did NOT terminate the probe: it moved it to the background at 5 s and the probe kept running and exited on its own.  The recorded text also says the probe 'wrote no file', but the tool wrote its own owned output file for the backgrounded command.  The probe therefore demonstrates a BACKGROUND YIELD, not a kill, and it proves no terminating enforcement of the cap and no enclosing kill guarantee of any kind.

the_actual_facts.the_command_was: an ad hoc probe that is NOT one of the frozen literal tool inputs of the plan
the_actual_facts.the_result_content: Command did not complete within its 5s timeout and was moved to the background (ID: bqf273a7s). Output is being written to: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-orca-workspaces-LocalViewWorkbench-lvw-v1-d0-implement/425850b4-055a-47b8-9dba-d311b90b2440/tasks/bqf273a7s.output. You will be notified when it completes. To check interim output, use Read on that file path.
the_actual_facts.the_tool_action: the command did not complete within its 5 s timeout and the tool MOVED IT TO THE BACKGROUND; the tool did not kill it and the tool did not wait for it
the_actual_facts.the_natural_completion: the two date outputs of the probe are 6.003442606 s apart and the tool recorded '[exited with code 0]': the probe completed NATURALLY after the background yield and it was not terminated
the_actual_facts.no_leak_is_alleged: no leaked process, no unknown cleanup and no resource leak is alleged for this simple probe: its own terminal output proves the natural exit and the exit code 0
the_actual_facts.what_it_touched: the probe ran no candidate code, it imported nothing, it compiled nothing, it collected nothing and it ran no test, and it read and wrote nothing of the report root, of the counter or of any product data; the only file it produced is the TOOL OWNED output file of the backgrounded command, which the tool wrote and not the probe
the_actual_facts.what_the_probe_does_NOT_prove: it does NOT prove that a cap of 5000 ms terminates a command, it does NOT prove an enclosing kill or reap guarantee of any kind, and in particular it establishes NO terminating owner for the 290 s envelope of the guard

the_wrong_statements.the_label: the configured caps of the five calls
the_wrong_statements.the_recorded_text: 5000, 290000, 5000, 5000 and 5000 milliseconds were the timeout parameters that the five calls really carried
the_wrong_statements.why_it_is_wrong: the statement is TRUE about the parameter and it must not be read as a statement about a stop guarantee.  The timeout PARAMETER of the five calls was exactly 5000, 290000, 5000, 5000 and 5000 milliseconds and that is a fact of the tool call metadata; a timeout parameter is not a termination owner, and this batch establishes no enclosing kill, no owned child identity, no bounded stop escalation and no reap.
the_wrong_statements.the_correction: the parameter equality stands and it is separated from the four different things that the review distinguishes: the equality of the timeout PARAMETER, the RETURN OR YIELD OR BACKGROUND action of the caller, the TERMINATION of the command tree, and the REAPING of the resources.  Only the first of the four is established for this batch.

the_wrong_statements.the_label: the relation between the elapsed time and the envelope
the_wrong_statements.the_recorded_text: the guard of this batch measured 55.397374868 s of wall time and the runner 55.284785271 s, and both are under the frozen 290 s cap.  An elapsed time that happens to be under a bound is NOT a proof that the bound was configured; the proof of this batch is the CONFIGURED parameter of the tool call, which is recorded above and which the independent review reads from the original call metadata of this batch.
the_wrong_statements.why_it_is_wrong: the recorded text is TRUE and it is incomplete.  The elapsed time is not a proof of the envelope, and neither is the configured timeout parameter: the recorded text of the probe in the same document claimed that the cap was 'enforced', and that claim was wrong because the probe was backgrounded and completed naturally.  The hard control of this batch is NOT ESTABLISHED.
the_wrong_statements.the_correction: the elapsed time under the cap proves neither the configuration nor the enforcement of a stop; the configured parameter proves the parameter and not the stop; and the probe of this batch proves that the tool yields to the background instead of killing.  The hard control of the combined02 checkpoint is NOT ESTABLISHED and the review of the root owns the remediation.
